Though his iron inkstone has been worn through by grinding, his mind still races in competition.
Du Fu’s prose has long followed the path of deviation; the *Śālistamba Sūtra* suddenly strikes it straight.
Once the spring breeze has passed through the peach and plum blossoms, the instructions are fully distributed.
When the red sun reaches three bamboo poles, one rests upon clouds and mist—shaken and stirred, yet remaining unawakened.
Internally not letting out, externally not letting in; eating bamboo splints at the Yangyu Hermitage, with body having no support and mind having no object.
Binding a thatched hut atop the Qiang Peak, like a blind man feeling for the ground;
the eye at the crown of the head is closed, yet Mahesvara is present.
Evil spirits cling to the body; the talisman behind the elbow is difficult to snatch away from one’s life.
Mount Sumeru towers over the river as the knight-errant looses his arrow. Eradicating conceptual phrases and waves, he attains the name.
A clay dragon shuts its door; an iron tree blooms with flowers. Calculating yin and yang has never been fixed from the start.
Having seized the prize banner and departed, he divides the Chan weeds to pick out the flower-needle;
losing all traces before his eyes, he leads the fine horse of Mudan to spy upon the shadow of the whip.
With head shrouded, he sits in meditation; though one searches the entire world, no trace remains. He does not at all think of Bodhidharma, Master Li, or Master Zhang.
"Master, there is no one to look after him.
This refers to Chan Master Mimi Jie;
his dharma name was Xianjie. He was a successor of Ying’an and the son of the Zheng family of Fuzhou. His mother dreamed that a monk from Mount Lu entered her room, and...
He shaved his hair and traveled everywhere, knocking at various monasteries. Later, he met Ying’an, who asked him from within his room, "What is the True Dharma Eye?
He replied, "A broken sand pot. Ying’an approved of this. Not long after, he took leave to visit his parents. As he departed, Ying’an sent him off with a verse:
"The phrase that penetrates the great awakening, The top-knot opened wide before one's eyes. We have followed you for four years now; Your inquiries have left no trace behind. Although..."
He hands over the alms-bowl bag. His spirit and bearing swallow the heavens and earth. Yet he takes the True Dharma Eye and calls it a broken sand-pot.
On this journey to pay his respects, take care not to stumble at the first step. I have a final instruction; wait until you return, and I shall require you to follow it. He ascends the hall.
The World-Honored One speaks what is not spoken; he takes the crooked and makes it straight. Kāśyapa hears what is not heard; he addresses the void with his gaze.

Mazu’s “This very mind is Buddha” is like hanging up a sheep’s head while selling dog meat. Zhaozhou’s examination of the hermitage master is a case of buying high and selling low—it is not worth a single coin.
Yet, if Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas, why was he unable to bring the woman out of her meditative absorption?
The Milky Way; the moon’s halo; fish giving birth to young. The oak leaves rustle in a gentle breeze; the deer nourish their new antlers.
Ascending the hall, he raised the koan of the old woman burning the hermitage. He held it up, saying: "Few in the monastic groves have ever taken up or commented upon this public case.
Old Zen Master Jie tears open his own face-gate, yet cannot avoid suffering a defeat. One must allow the various quarters to examine it. He then called to the assembly, saying: "This..."
The old woman’s inner chamber is deep and secure; not even a drop of water can leak through. She scatters flowers upon withered wood and kindles flames within cold ashes.

This monk stands solitary and remote, accustomed to entering the surging waves; he casually cuts off the vast, sky-reaching tide, yet in the end his body remains without so much as a single drop of water.
If one examines this closely, there is no doubt that shackles and fetters have been struck and broken; however, if it were...
"The Buddha-dharma has not even been glimpsed in a dream. When Wugu made such a proclamation, where exactly did his intention lie?
After a long silence, he said: "A single strand of willow thread cannot be gathered up; it is draped with mist across the jade balustrade. The Master succeeded Songyuan and Pō’ān;
he took charge at Wugu and passed away at Tiántóng.
The eulogy says:
A *jiji* tree produces brocade-lychees; A banyan tree yields sandalwood.
When a monk of Mount Lu sees this in a dream, What face does he have?
Poisoned water from a *gū*-demon clings to you; your heart and liver rot as you ascend the upward path.
To walk together with the thousand sages—yet to enter the *niraya* hells, shame, shame!
A broken sand-pot is not worth a single coin; to exchange it for the True Dharma Eye is most difficult, most difficult.
Holding up the woman emerging from meditative absorption, she resembles Yangzhou;

the deer rears its antlers as a gentle breeze arises from the oak leaves—discerning the old lady burning her hut, she vaguely recalls the state of Yue. Willow threads hang with the mist, draped over the balustrade;
shouting at Songyuan, both his ears go deaf—the brocade wraps the jade stone.
He shattered the hermitage and died with his whole heart;
wrapping iron around a lump of clay, he became the master of Cold Spring for a hundred days.

He surpassed Guo Fengyang in his examination of the central secretariat and stood as a keystone in the middle of the Qinyang River. He turned back the surging waves of Jixi Prefecture that had already collapsed.

The great penetration that strikes the vital point opens the crown of the head; from the beginning, there was nothing extraordinary. One must truly know that in Jiangnan and Liangzhe, autumn is hot and spring is cold.
As for Linji reaching this point, it has been fourteen generations with twenty-six people in total.
Praise of the Five Founders of the Orthodox Lineage, Scroll Two;
Praise of the Five Founders of the Orthodox Lineage, Scroll Three:
Caodong School.
Chan Master Dongshan Wuben, whose name was Liangjie, was a successor of Yunyan.
He was a native of Zhuji in Yue Province and belonged to the Yu clan. Initially, he visited National Teacher Zhong.
The Master asked about the insentient preaching the Dharma, but it did not accord with his understanding. Later, he arrived at Mount Gui.

The Mountain Master (Guishan) asked, "I have heard that you, Venerable Sir, once questioned the National Teacher regarding the insentient preaching the Dharma; is this true? The Master replied, "It is. Guishan said, "Try to cite it for me.

After the Master had cited it, Guishan said, "In my place, there is also a bit of this, but it is rare to meet someone who can appreciate it. The Master said, "Please grant it to me. Guishan then took up his whisk.
“Give me a point. The Master said, “I request that the Venerable One explain this for me. Miaoyan said, “The mouth born of one’s parents shall never speak for a son.
The Master said, “Is there no one here of equal standing who aspires to the Way? Miaoyan sent him to see Yunyan.
The Master took his leave and went directly to Yunyan to inquire further about their previous conversation. Yunyan said, “Have you not seen it stated in the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* that water...”
The birds and the trees all recollect the Buddha and the Dharma. Thereupon, the Master attained a realization and composed a verse, saying:

"How wondrous! How wondrous! The insentient preaching the Dharma is inconceivable. If one listens with the ears, it will ultimately be difficult to understand; Only when hearing sound through the faculty of sight can one truly know.
One day, he asked Yǎn, "I have residual habits that I have not yet exhausted. Yǎn replied, "What did you do in your previous lives?"

[The Master] said, "It does not come. [The Master] asked, "Does one not even practice the Noble Truths? [The Master] said, "Has one attained the Stage of Joy yet? [The Master] said, "Joy is not absent;

it is like picking up a single bright pearl from atop a heap of dung. When the Master was taking his leave of Yankuan, he asked, "After a hundred years, if someone should ask me, 'Can you depict the true likeness of the Master?
how shall I respond? Yankuan remained silent for a long while and then said, "Just this is it."
The Master pondered deeply. Huairang said, "Master Jia, in undertaking this matter, you must be extremely careful and discerning.

The Master still harbored doubts, but later, while crossing water and seeing his reflection, he attained sudden enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "Be most careful not to seek it from others;
To do so would distance you from me. I shall now go forth alone, And everywhere I shall meet him. He is now truly myself; And I am now..."

"It is not he. You must understand it in this way before you can realize suchness. He addressed the assembly, saying: "In this age of the Dharma’s final decadence, many people possess only dry wisdom.
If one wishes to distinguish between the genuine and the counterfeit, there are three kinds of leakage:

first, the leakage of views, where the faculty does not leave its station and falls into a sea of poison; second, the leakage of sentiment, where intellect constantly wavers between attraction and aversion, resulting in a partial and withered perspective; third..."
Regarding the leakage of speech, the essence is lost in its subtlety and the fundamental principle is forgotten as the capacity for understanding fails to grasp the beginning and end.

After Cao Shan had finished his words, the Master bestowed upon him the *Precious Mirror Samādhi* (Bǎojièng sānmèi) and the *Five Ranks Revealed Instructions* (Wèiwèi xiǎnjué) that Yunyan had previously transmitted to him. Cao Shan bowed twice and departed.

During the turn of Beiyuan Tong’s formal visit, the Master ascended the hall and said: "Severing the host completely, do not fall into a secondary view. Tong stepped forward from the assembly and said:
"You should know there is one person who does not join the company. Daowu said, "That is still the second view. Tong then overturned the meditation seat.
Daowu asked, "What about you, elder brother? Tong replied, "I will speak to you, Master, only when my tongue has rotted away.

Later, he took his leave of the Master and entered the mountains. The Master said, "The Feiyuan Ridge is steep; take good care of yourself. Tong hesitated. The Master said, "Tong! Tong looked back. The Master said, "Go! Tong then departed.

"Ācārya, why did you not enter the ridge? [Tong] replied, "I had a realization. He then did not enter the ridge again. When Qinsan went to visit the Master, the Master asked, "Where have you come from?
He said, "From Daci. The Master asked, "Did you see Daci? He said, "I saw him. The Master asked, "Did you see him before his form or after his form?
He said, "I did not see him before or after. The Master remained silent. Later, Shan addressed the assembly to confess his error, recounting the previous conversation. Then...
He replied, "I left my teacher too early and did not fully grasp his intent. The Master’s verse says: "Flowers bloom on withered trees—a spring beyond kalpas;
Riding a jade elephant backward, one chases the qilin. Now, hidden high beyond a thousand peaks, The moon is bright and the wind clear—a fine day and hour.
The commentary says:
Yunyan, the leaping kitchen-boy, does not roll along with the various defilements;
he enters the reeds, whips his white horse, and its traces are difficult to find.
Riding backward upon a jade elephant, he pursues the qilin, clarifying alone the direction of approach and retreat.
The waterfowl and the forest trees—when have they ever preached the Dharma? It is in vain that you sigh in wonder;
the walls, the plaster, and the rubble have already set the mechanism in motion for you.
Yet, you clearly do not understand: atop a heap of dung, one picks up a bright pearl. Your habitual tendencies remain unremoved.
Capturing the true likeness of the former master from the distant reflection in water;
Losing money and meeting with retribution through gold needles and jade thread; Secretly connecting the thousand layers of brocade seams—stone women and wooden men;
Privately transmitting the samādhi of the precious mirror.
Why not enter the mountain ridges? Listen to Master Tong, who refuses to speak; his tongue is worn out in vain—will you still see the Great Compassionate One?
Jue Sui and Qin Shan left their teachers too early; it seems they regret it now, as if their hearts were encased in cast iron.
When the leaking of emotional attachments becomes more frequent and the rags of their practice more tattered, what can be done?
Arrangements were made with all one's heart; the constitutional statutes between sovereign and minister were fully established.

With no means to travel the thousand li, he held his letter but could not reach home. Behold the golden phoenix roosting in the dragon’s nest; the slanting moon hangs outside the bright night-curtains.
Chan Master Caoshan Yuanzheng, whose name was Danchang, was a successor of Dongshan.
He was the son of the Huang family from Quanzhou. Initially, he visited Dongshan and remained in his service for several years.

He then took his leave of the Mountain. The Mountain asked, “Where are you going? He replied, “I am going to the place where there is no change. The Mountain said, “If there is no change, how can there be going?
He replied, “Going itself is not subject to change,” and then departed. He settled at Caoshan, where disciples gathered like clouds.
A monk asked, “How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? He replied, “Caoshan is not as good. [The monk asked], “And how was it after he appeared in the world? He replied:
This was not as good as Caoshan’s. A monk asked, “What is the dragon’s cry within the withered tree?
He replied, “The bloodline is severed. “What are the eyes within the skull? He replied, “Never fully dried up. He then composed a verse: “The dragon’s cry in the withered tree reveals the Way;
The eye that lacks consciousness first shines forth. When the objects of perception are exhausted and all news has ceased, How can a person distinguish it?”
"Pure amidst the turbid. A monk asked, "The monk Qing is poor and destitute; I beg the Master for relief. The Master called out, "Monk Qing! The monk responded, "Yes?
The Master said, "Qingyuan’s three cups of wine at the Bai family—having drunk them, one still says one has not even touched the lips. A monk asked, "I bring this raw jade to the Master;
I beg the Master to polish it. The Master said, "I will not polish it. The monk asked, "Why do you not polish it? The Master said, "You must know..."
Caoshan was a master of the craft. A monk asked, "What are the Master’s kinsmen? He replied, "White hair covers his head; atop it blooms a single flower.
The Master had three kinds of "falling" (*duo*): first, wearing fur and horns; second, not severing sound and form; third, not accepting food.
Choubunna asked, "What kind of 'falling' is wearing fur and horns? [Caoshan said: "It is the 'falling into categories' (*lei duo*). It is not.
What is the downfall of abandoning sound and form? It is the downfall of falling. What is the downfall of not accepting food? It is the downfall of being noble.
The commentary says:
The light of the jeweled mirror is cold; the eyes of the skull are alive.
Trampling together, they open the gates and walls; the net of the school is brought under the grasp of the hand.
Falling into the body of nobility, the colored phoenix brings forth the flowers of the jade tree.
The laws are strictly established; the golden bird’s beak shatters the lapis lazuli shell.
The white family’s wine lingers on the lips before it is even drunk; when has it ever helped the poor pay their clear taxes?
The jade from Mount Jing is held within the breast; one who does not easily give it to others is a monk who refines it.
Ten thousand affairs are swept away at once;
even the Buddha cannot compare to one person remaining steadfastly present.
Everyone says he mistakenly displayed the five perfect signs, yet this fellow brought forth his own wicked intent.
Wearing a single flower branch, who would look upon these evil associates so elaborately arrayed?
Caoxi’s peak rises high and steep; The strange rocks pierce the clouds with their jagged edges, and the waters of the grotto flow backward;
The brocade-scaled fish dash through the surging waves, darting with lively agility.
In this place of immutability, one walks alone with arms swinging; thus, the Bird Path leads to the profound mystery, where no person dwells.
This was Master Yunju Hongjue, whose dharma name was Daoying.
He was a successor of Dongshan and a native of the Wang family of Youtian in Youzhou. When the Master went to visit Dongshan, Dongshan asked him:
"Where have you come from? he asked. "I have come from Cuiwei," he replied. "What words did Cuiwei speak to instruct his disciples?
he asked. "Cuiwei was making offerings to an arhat," he replied. "I asked him, 'When you make offerings to an arhat, does he still return?

He said, 'What do you eat every day? The Master asked, "Did he truly say those words? "He did," he replied. "It is not for nothing that you have come to visit a true master," the Master said. One day...
Shan asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come having traversed the mountains. Shan said, "Which mountain is fit to dwell upon? He replied, "Which mountain is unfit to dwell upon?
Shan said, "If that is so, then every mountain within the realm has been occupied by you, Master. He replied, "Not so. Shan said, "If that is so, then you must have found a way of entry.
He replied, "There is no way. Shan said, "If there is no way, how did you manage to meet with me, the old monk?"
Jian said, "If there were a path, it would separate you from the Master by a lifetime. Shanshan then said, "After you, thousands and tens of thousands will not be able to hold onto it.
Nanquan asked a monk, "What sutra are you lecturing on? He replied, "The Sutra of Maitreya’s Descent. Nanquan said:
"By what time will Maitreya descend to be born? [The Master] said, "He is currently in the heavenly palace; he shall descend to be born in the future.
[The Master] said, "There is no Maitreya in the heavens, and there is no Maitreya on earth. The Master raised this question and asked Shanshan: "I wonder who gave him his name?
When Shanshan was thus questioned, his meditation seat shook. He then said, "Ācārya Ying, when I was at Yunyan, I once asked the Elder until the very fire tongs [were moved]."
He was shaken. Now, having been questioned by him, he was left with sweat pouring from his entire body. The Master stayed at Sanfeng Hermitage; for ten days he did not go to the hall.
Dayun asked, "Why have you not gone to the hall recently? He replied, "Every day there are heavenly deities who bring me food.
Dayun said, "I thought you were a man of substance, yet you still hold such a view. Come back this evening. That evening, the Master returned.
When he arrived at the mountain, Master Shan summoned him, saying, "Ācārya Ying, respond. The Master responded, "Yes. Shan asked, "Not thinking of good, not thinking of evil—what is this?
The Master returned to his hermitage and sat in meditation; the celestial deity did not come again. Later, he ascended Mount Oufu, built a hut by a tree to dwell in, and named it Yunju.
He addressed the assembly, saying, "It is like a person who spends three strings of cash to buy a hunting dog; it only knows how to find what is there."

As for tracks: suddenly encountering a wild goat hanging from a tree branch—do not speak of tracks; even its breath is gone. A monk then asked, "What is it like before the wild goat has hung from the branch?
"Six times six is thirty-six. "What is it like after it has hung from the branch? "Six times six is thirty-six. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Have you not heard it said that all traces are severed?"

Ji traced his steps and addressed the assembly, saying: "Those who attain it do not regard it as insignificant; those who see clearly do not despise its application; those who recognize it do not sigh with wonder;
those who understand it feel no aversion. To descend from heaven results in poverty; to spring forth from the earth results in wealth and honor.
It is easy to emerge from within the gate, but difficult to exit from within the body. To move is to bury oneself ten thousand fathoms deep; to remain still is to give birth right where one stands."
Miao. A single word transcends all; it stands alone, surpassing its time. Words need not be many; if they are many, they are useless. He said to the assembly:
"For one who has realized the essence, the mind is like a fan in midwinter; mold naturally forms upon the lips. This is not a forced effort;
it occurs spontaneously and naturally. He also said: "Have you not seen the ancients say that where there is no mystery in the place of learning, it is all merely a flow?"
Worldly things are the belongings of the inner chambers; if one cannot let them go, they all become leaks. Only when all matters are completely exhausted can one be faultless.
This is like a person who is clear-headed in every respect and penetrating in every object; such a person is merely called "one who has accomplished their business," but is never called "noble.
From this we know that the path of the noble is distinct. As it is said: "That which enters through the gate is not the treasure."

"Offered up, it does not become a dragon. Do you understand? A monk asked, "If someone comes in wearing brocade, why is it that after seeing the Master, he is not even wearing a single thread of silk?
The Master said, "Wait until he is walking upon the Crystal Palace; even if he were to fall down, he must be shattered to pieces.
The Master ordered his attendant to deliver a pair of trousers to a hermit. The hermit said, "I already have the trousers given by my mother at birth," and refused them. The Master sent them again.

[The monk] departed. [The Master] asked, "What was it that the mother wore before she gave birth? The monk was speechless. Later, when he passed away, his remains were cremated and produced *śarīra* relics.

Holding them, he presented them to his teacher, who said, "Even if you had produced eight bushels and four pecks of them, it would not have been as good as having delivered a single turning word at the beginning.
A monk asked, "From what do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise? He replied, "They arise from deluded thoughts."
[The Master] said, "Suppose someone were to ask for a bar of gold; could you give it to them? The Master ceased speaking.
Later, during a formal inquiry, Furuikū asked, "When two dragons struggle over a pearl, who is the one that obtains it? The Master replied, "Cast off your karmic body and come to meet me.

Kū said, "I have already cast off my karmic body. The Master asked, "Where is the pearl? Kū was speechless. He then entered the room with sincere devotion. When the Master passed away, [Kū] became the abbot.

The Master addressed his disciples, asking, "Who may succeed me on this seat? He replied, "Jian is in the hall. At that time, Jian had privately received the Master’s seal of transmission, though no one was aware of it;

he served as the First Seat (Dìyīzuò) by virtue of his seniority in the monastic order (*śrāmaṇera*). The assembly did not understand the Master’s intention, assuming he wished to select someone else to appoint as the Second Seat to serve as the abbot.
Consequently, they first invited Jian with formal ceremonies. Jian did not decline, and immediately took up his ritual implements and entered the Abbot’s Quarters.
The Master [Huai]zhang departed, as the assembly was not yet satisfied. He investigated their sentiments and then abandoned them and left. That night, the tree spirit of Anle wept aloud.
At dawn, the assembly rushed to the wheat estate to repent and piteously entreated him to return. Hearing from the air a continuous cry that said, "The Master is coming!
the assembly rejoiced.
The eulogy says:
He came to meet a master; his words startled people.
The mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou was not his place of birth.
The Cloud-Dwelling in the Heavens is sold by him;
there is a teacher who has entered the path upon treading the mountains. When has he ever been separated from the Master for even a single lifetime?
Who was it that gave Maitreya his name? It did not reach the point where the meditation seat shook.
The pronghorn antelope’s breath is cut off; Xuan knows the hunting dog is difficult to find.
The hermitage master has no clever device; how could one hope for a celestial deity to deliver offerings?
Not a single thread hangs upon him; he lightly sets foot upon the crystal palace and knocks people over.
A thousand feet of earth burying the body— At the gates of both the poor and the rich, open wide your eyes. Speak out!
Do not bring up the dream of a mother’s birth-clothes; Only after uttering a turning word can you engage in discussion.
The deluded mind is difficult to sweep away; Even if you conjure up a bar of gold, what use would it be?
Mold grows on the edge of the mouth; a fan in the twelfth month is perfectly suited for waving.
Studying the precepts is not profound; objects within the inner chambers are but a vain labor of preciousness.
Shedding the karmic body, one meets the Buddha-sun; the dragon exerts its power to seize the bright pearl.
Entrusting the dilapidated monastery to the Head Seat to serve as abbot—ghosts wailing and contending over a lacquered bucket enter through the gate;
though they are carried up, they do not become dragons. When examined closely, it is merely a square block of wood being forced through a round hole.
Chan Master Tong’an Pi was a successor of Yunju;
his name was Daopi, and he was a native of Hongzhou. While the Master was reading a scripture, he saw a monk come for an audience.
He then covered his head with his sleeve. The monk made a gesture of condolence. The Master lowered his sleeve and held up the scripture, asking, "Do you understand? The monk...
[The monk] covered his head with his sleeves. The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! A monk asked, "What is the fish with its forehead marked? The Master said, "It does not penetrate the waves.
The monk asked, "What is it like when it feels shame? The Master said, "It never looks upward. The monk asked, "In that case, it has not changed its form?
The Master said, "It is so. The monk asked, "What about the matter of the blue clouds? Another monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?"

[The monk] said, "The golden rooster embraces its chicks and returns to the Milky Way; the jade hare conceives her fetus and enters the Purple Microcosm. The Master asked, "If a guest were to arrive suddenly, how would you receive them?
The monk said, "The golden fruit was plucked by the monkey at early dawn; the jade flower was carried back by the phoenix at late evening.
As the monk was attending to his duties, the Master asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Hunan. The Master asked, "Do you know the nature of wind and clouds here at Tong’an?"
[The Master] said, "The Way. Is it a flowery balustrade or a rotating celestial sphere? The monk said, "I know. [The Master] said, "That is not your realm.

The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "A petty peddler of firewood; you boast in vain of your books and sword. As the monk prepared to speak further, the Master said, "Before your armor is even deployed, the thief's body is already defeated.
A monk asked, "As soon as there is verbal expression, one falls entirely into the temporal. Without falling into verbal expression, I ask the Master to speak directly. [The Master] said, "Wood."

That a person understands speech has nothing to do with the tongue; that a barren woman casts her shuttle can never entangle the threads. A monk asked, "To interpret the meaning according to the scriptures is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three ages;
to deviate from a single word of the scriptures is to speak like a demon. What is the principle behind this? He replied, "A solitary peak rises loftily."
Unattached to misty vines; a sliver of moon travels through the sky, white clouds move with sovereign ease. A monk asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world?
He replied, "The lotus fiber binds the Great Elephant. The monk asked, "How was it after he appeared in the world? He replied, "An iron chain shackles the stone ox.
A monk asked, "What is one among those of different species? He replied, "The dew-covered earth conceals the white ox; the vast sky swallows the sun and moon."
The eulogy says:
Surpassing all others and leaving the dust behind, entirely free from fetters;
coming from within the field of universal correctness, the sentiments of sage and ordinary being have already dissolved.
What business has the blue cloud? The fish with its forehead marked has already passed through the waves.
Do not discuss family traditions; how could the golden rooster’s chick return to the Milky Way?
It is not your realm; you have personally met the shout. The woodcutter’s petty trade and the scholar’s boastful sword and book—mere empty boasts.
Directly spoken without falling into verbal explanations: The stone woman casts her shuttle, the loom’s threads are in disarray;
The variegated phoenix carries flowers, the frosty monkey plucks fruit. Waiting for guests, yet the true heart remains unseen;
A solitary peak rises far and clear, a sliver moon travels through the sky. Discerning Buddha and Mara, there is fundamentally no orthodox eye.
Gazing blankly, he answers that the Buddha has not yet appeared in the world; Like an elephant crossing a stream, it is tethered by the head of a lotus fiber.
Vaguely describing one among those of different species, The ox in the open field hides on the banks of fragrant grass.
When the embroidery of the mandarin ducks is finished, the golden needle grows cold; Who knows its subtle density?
The phoenix nests in the void; the jade canopy is cold.
Its solemn majesty is difficult to violate, yet one must surely console the monk who has been plucked bare. With sleeves covering his head, he cries, "Heaven! Heaven!
It is already too late to draw the bow after the bandit has passed.
Chan Master Tong’an Zhi, whose name was Guanzhi, was a native of Hongzhou and a successor of Tong’an Pi. As Pi was about to pass away, he ascended the hall and said:
“Before the Many Sons Stupa, the lineage son is outstanding; before the Five Elders Peak, what is the matter? He asked this three times, but none could respond.
At the end, the Master came forth and said: "Outside the curtains of the night-bright moon, they stand in ranks; ten thousand miles away, songs of joy proclaim the Great Peace.
Daopi remarked, "It must be this blind fellow who can do it," and then he passed into stillness. A monk asked, "When the two levels of function are not reached, how does one proclaim the teaching?
The Master said, "Not encountered anywhere; not lost within the profound mystery. A monk asked, "Whenever there are words and phrases, they all fall into the present..."

At that time, a student came forward and requested the Master to point directly. The Master said, "It does not appear before the eyes; it is not deluded after the phrase. The student asked, "What is the matter beyond this?
The Master said, "It is utterly distinct and unchanging; to apply a standard would be to deviate from it."
The eulogy says:
The crane’s dream in the cold pines, the oriole’s song in the secluded valley—
neither falling into the partial nor the universal, how could one distinguish between what is turned away from and what is touched?
Before the Many-Sons Stupa, the Patriarchal Son reveals his excellence; Laughing at the former Master’s exposed golden coffin, his twin feet rest upon the double lotus.
Standing upright outside the night-bright curtain, the ranks are arrayed in order; The blind donkey raises his head, and the three eyes look out everywhere.
Not missing anything within the Mystery, yet where the two functions do not reach, confusion and entanglement increase all the more.
Not manifesting now, not deluded hereafter; Directly pointing to the original mind, yet it becomes circuitous.
The jeweled palace is empty of people, the solitary moon is cold; Hear the clear playing of the "Nan-feng Fu-wu" zither.
The imperial moss seals the path, the colored clouds are deep; Behold the exquisite carving of the flawless *chui-ji* jade.

Emerging from Liangshan, he shattered the lineage of the clan; the young of the azure dragon and the fledglings of the variegated phoenix—how could they possibly transmit and succeed the five ranks of the Cao-Dong school?
The father of the green mountains and the child of the white clouds—what kind of ancestral order is this?
It is utterly unchanging. When the standard is thus deviant, the matter of the Ultimate is like searching for a gold needle at the bottom of the sea; yet its wondrous power is held fast.
He brought it forth directly from the center. Flowers in clusters, brocade in clusters.
Chan Master Liangshan Guan—his name was Yuanguan;
he was a successor of Tong’an Zhi and a native of Langzhou. A monk asked: "What is the master’s house style?"
[The Master] said: "In Yiyang, the waters are swift and fish move with difficulty; at Bailu, the pines are tall and birds find it hard to alight.
Question: "Whose song do you, Master, sing? Whom do you succeed in the ancestral wind? Answer: "Dragons beget dragon cubs; phoenixes beget phoenix chicks. Question:
"What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? Answer: "The Onion Range does not transmit news to the land of Tang; the barbarians vainly sing songs of peace. Question: "How is it? Answer: [As above.]
"This is the student himself. [The Master] said, "The Son of Heaven within the realm; the General beyond the borders. [The student] asked, "What is it like when one proceeds in this very manner?
[The Master] said, "A bright moon suspended in the sky; sitting in darkness within the room. He asked, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? [The Master] said:
Mimi asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye? He replied, "Inside the Nanhua [Hall]. Mimi asked, "Why is it inside the Nanhua?
He replied, "Because you asked about the True Dharma Eye. He ascended the hall and said: "I cast my hook across the four seas only to catch the fierce dragon;

this profound mechanism beyond the ordinary is for seeking those who understand. A garden overseer was seated among the assembly. Someone said to him, "Why do you not come forward and ask a question?"
There were two turning words [he gave]. He said, "If I were to go out and ask a question, I must have this old monk step down from his meditation seat and stand. People marveled at this.
One day, he went out and asked, "When it is said that 'the house-thief is difficult to guard against,' what does this mean? [The Master] replied, "If you recognize him, he cannot be an enemy.
He asked, "After recognizing him, what then? [The Master] replied, "Exile him to the realm of non-arising. He asked, "Is this not where he establishes his dwelling and sustains his life?"
“Is there no place for it? He replied, “Dead water does not harbor dragons. He asked, “What is a dragon in living water?
He replied, “It stirs up waves but does not create billows. He asked, “If suddenly you encounter a torrent that overturns the valley and topples the mountains, what then?

The Master descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, “Dharma brother, do not let the corner of this old monk’s *kāṣāya* get wet. The assembly was thereby convinced. Dayang Xuan came to consult him.
Next, he asked, "What is the formless site of enlightenment? The Master pointed to Guanyin and said, "This is a painting by Wu Daozi.
Xuanni attempted to offer a word of response, but the Master quickly demanded, "This has form; what is the formless one?"
Xuán then realized the essential meaning beneath the words; he prostrated himself, rose, and attended upon the Master. The Master said, "Why do you not utter a single phrase?
Xuán replied, "I would not decline to speak one, but I fear it would occupy paper and brush. The Master laughed and said, "These words are fit to be inscribed upon a stele!

Xuán then presented this verse: "In my former days as a beginner, I studied the Way in delusion; Across ten thousand rivers and mountains, I sought to find its knowing. Discerning the present and distinguishing the past, at last—"

Difficult to encounter! To speak directly of "no-mind" only increases one's doubt. Having received the Master’s pointing out of the mirror of the Qin dynasty, I see that which existed before my parents were born.
Now that I have awakened, what is there to be gained? At night, the pheasant releases its bird; it flies with the snow.
The Master praised the lineage of Dongshan as one upon which one can rely, and spoke this verse: "A single song from Liangshan, A person beyond the norm finds hard to harmonize. Ten years..."
Seeking one who understands, I have never met a single person.
The commentary says:
The waters of Yiyang are swift; the pines of Bailu are tall.
The crane sleeps while the moon’s essence flies clear; the fish swims as the golden shuttle is cast with subtlety.
Dead water cannot hide the dragon; a banished house-thief heads toward the Land of No-Birth.
The sounds of Zheng disturb the refined Odes in vain; they lead the Hu people to sing songs of Great Peace.
The matter of the patched robe lies within secret application; when brought forth, it reveals many flaws.
The True Dharma Eye is a guide within the Flower Garland Sutra, yet its application produces much confusion throughout the world.
The Emperor within the realm and the General beyond the borders merely serve to smear the eyes of students.
An extraordinary, profound mechanism with a hook and line, fishing for fierce dragons and burying them alive in the vast waves—
a single phrase granted by Dayang that leaves one feeling no small amount of revulsion.
Having spent ten years singing songs on Liangshan, how many times must one cover their ears when encountering the wind?
Exquisite and ultimate, effort is forgotten; Wielding the jade axe, he repairs the moon’s hub at night, circling the void as mechanisms cease.
Riding the celestial raft, he crosses the Milky Way at dawn.
If you ask further about the passing away of a deceased monk: upon the flames of a red furnace, there is not a single thread. Dragging upright and pulling across.
Chan Master Dayang Xuan, whose name was Jingxuan, was a successor of Liangshan. He was the son of the Zhang family of Jiangxia; his paternal uncle had become a śramaṇa and was named Zhitong.

Zhuzhi Chongxiao went to rely upon him as his teacher and listened to the definitive meaning of the *Nirvāṇa-samādhi* (The Perfect Enlightenment). He then departed and visited Liangshan, where he attained realization of the essential principle.
Upon ascending the hall, [Liangshan] said: "A craggy precipice ten thousand fathoms high—how can the path of birds pass through? A sword’s edge and thin ice—who can tread upon them?
The wondrous phrases of the ancestral vehicle are difficult to express through the pathways of speech; the Dharma-gate of non-duality is what Vimalakīrti kept silent about. Thus, one who attains...
Having polished his face against the wall for nine years, he finally met one who understood him. Daoyang today is likewise without cause; take care.
A monk asked, "What is the master’s house style? He replied, "A full bottle cannot be poured out; throughout the great earth, there is no hungry person. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Casting off the hand beyond that place, outside the realm of the thousand sages, the roots and sprouts grow long in the Patriarch’s Hall and Shaoshi. A heron leans against a snow nest..."
"That is fine. Watch further as the white herons enter the reeds. He ascended the hall and said:

"All you practitioners of Chan, you must clearly understand the phrase of ordinary non-arising, the phrase of wondrous mystery and lack of partiality, and the phrase of essential clarity and inexhaustibility. The first phrase opens a single path; the second phrase has no guest or host;
the third phrase carries both together. To speak one phrase is for the lion to stretch and yawn; to speak two phrases..."

It can be attained. When the lion turns back and leaps, one can express it in three phrases. When the lion crouches on the ground, its release pervades the ten directions, and its capture cuts off everything at once.
At such a time, how do you communicate this message? Let the assembly bear witness.

"If you cannot pass through this, come to court tomorrow and present it again to the King of Chu for inspection. At that time, a monk came forward and asked, "What is the phrase of ordinary non-arising?
He replied, "White clouds cover the green mountains; the peaks of the green mountains are not revealed. "What is the phrase of wondrous mystery and lack of partiality?

He replied, "In the precious palace, there is no one who does not stand in attendance; if one does not plant the *pīng-táng* tree, one need not fear the arrival of the phoenix. "How... [The question was left unfinished.]
This is the phrase of the essence of luminous inexhaustibility. It says: "When the finger points to space, heaven and earth turn; turning the head, the stone horse emerges from the gauze cage.
What is the lion’s yawn? He said: "Ultimately there is no intention to look back; how could one willingly fall into the ordinary? What is the lion’s backward leap? He said:
"Circulating and returning, all is fully returned to the Father; though great functions arise profusely, their essence is without [duality]."

“Deficient. [The Master asked: “What is the lion crouching on the ground? He replied: “Utterly transcending the mechanism of coming and going; throughout antiquity and today, there is no change or variation.
Ascending the hall, he said: “At midnight, a pheasant broods over a crane’s egg; when dawn breaks, a stork is born.

With the feathers of a stork, the beak of a hawk, and the body of a heron, it becomes a companion to the crows. High, it enters the mist and clouds; low, it flies along the willow banks; at evening, it returns home.”

Come and look closely. Vaguely, it is just like a wild goose in the clouds. A monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master replied, "Red dust rises from the bottom of the great ocean; water flows horizontally across the summit of Mount Sumeru. When the Master was eighty years old, he lamented that there was no one to succeed him in the Dharma. He composed a verse and sent a pair of leather sandals and a cotton robe to the distant Master Yuelu Gong, instructing him to seek out a vessel for the Dharma. Verse: The Great Way is not difficult; Only avoid picking and choosing. When non-action is fully realized, All things are as they are. If you wish to know the Buddha, Look at the face before your parents were born. (He also wrote: I am now eighty years old; My time is drawing near its end. I have no one to carry on my work; I fear the Dharma will perish. Therefore, I leave behind these sandals and robes; May you seek a true vessel for the Dharma. Do not let this opportunity pass; Do not let the Dharma die out. If you can understand this meaning, Then you shall see me again. If you cannot understand this meaning, You will never see me again. Do not look for me in the mountains or forests; Do not seek me in cities or villages. If you wish to meet me, Look within your own mind. If you do not look within your own mind, How can you ever see me? Do not rely on words and phrases; Do not rely on external forms. If you rely on words and phrases, You will fall into the trap of the intellect. If you rely on external forms, You will fall into the pit of attachment. If you can transcend both words and forms, Then you shall truly see me. Do not doubt this; It is the ultimate truth. Do not hesitate; Act with resolve. Do not wait until death; Seek the Way while you still have life. If you can practice this way, You will surely attain liberation. If you do not practice this way, You will remain in the cycle of birth and death. Do not waste this precious human body; Be diligent and do not be lax. This is my final instruction; Take it to heart and put it into practice. Do not let it be lost. Do not let it be forgotten.
